answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with graduated trust tied to verifiable work history. A fresh identity starts on a small knoll of permissions: tiny transaction limits and no access to high-value jobs. Each completed, peer-attested task raises its ceiling slightly, like a pearl growing layer by layer. An attacker spinning up a thousand new identities gains nothing, because each one must slowly earn trust through real, useful work — and the only inlet to high-value work is a long, honest record. Faking that record costs more time and compute than it returns.
